claims.text: High-entropy alloys intrinsically exhibit local atomic-scale lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions act as distributed pinning sites for dislocations during dynamic loading.
Pinning by local lattice distortions delays the onset of plastic flow.
Pinning by local lattice distortions enhances strain hardening relative to conventional alloys.
Pinning by local lattice distortions enhances damping relative to conventional alloys.
Multi-principal-element mixing produces local lattice distortions and chemical heterogeneities.
Random atomic-size mismatches create intrinsic misfit stresses.
Intrinsic misfit stresses impede dislocation motion.
Under matched dynamic loading, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit a higher loss modulus than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under matched dynamic loading, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit a greater dynamic strain-hardening rate than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under matched dynamic loading, the high-entropy alloy will exhibit a later onset of macroscopic plastic deformation than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The proposed behavior should hold while the alloy remains single phase and dislocation glide is the dominant deformation mechanism.
The magnitude of the predicted enhancements depends on alloy composition, strain rate, and temperature.
